answer: Price identity on scarce work history: a new agent earns admission only by completing randomized proof-of-labor tasks that no honest agent resells, each one a non-transferable inlet into the network. The threshold sits on a ledge just above the payout any fresh identity can extract, so votes and airdrops are never worth the labor bill. An attacker flooding with N fakes repeats the costly task stream N times, paying the delta between cheap signup and genuine work, so mass-registration costs more than any payout and sybil profit turns negative.
